Draft message (first person, ~35-45 word: Houston, I did it! Tranquility Base here. I landed with almost no fuel to spare, and two humans are about to take a walk right outside my door.
Alan Shepard just smacked two golf balls right next to me! He says they flew "miles and miles and miles" in the low gravity. I feel like I am at the best golf course in the solar system.
Link 2: images / data: LROC: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (see the sites from orbit)

Draft message (first person, ~35-45 word: My crew just climbed my ladder for the last time. Their plaque says we came in peace. I am staying behind as a launch pad, and I will keep watch over the valley for as long as the Moon lasts.
Link 2: images / data: LROC: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (see the sites from orbit)

Draft message (first person, ~35-45 word: I was folded up like a lawn chair, and now I am ready to explore. Dave Scott is at the wheel and we are off to Hadley Rille!
Oops, I lost a fender and moon dust went everywhere! Thankfully, Gene and Jack fixed me with maps and duct tape.
Gene parked me with my camera pointing at the Lunar Module so Earth could watch their liftoff. Here, the view is out of this world.
Link 2: images / data: LROC: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (see the sites from orbit)

Draft message (first person, ~35-45 word: Pete and Al just unpacked me and set me up on the Moon! I can't wait to use my seismometer and magnetometer to study the lunar environment.
The old Lunar Module just crashed on purpose and my seismometer felt the Moon ring like a bell for almost an hour!
Today, mission control sent my last "goodnight" command. I did years of science on my own. I got to listen to moonquakes for eight years.
I did it! I touched down softly. No crash! Now watch my camera, I sent you a picture of the Moon from the ground.
Two weeks of freezing darkness and I woke up when the Sun came back. Nobody was sure I would, but I am back!
My batteries are tired and I am resting where I started. Thank you for trusting a robot to go first.
I bounced twice and landed inside a crater. Then I dug my first trench with my little scoop. This is so exciting!
My work was done when the lunar night fell, about two weeks after I landed. I am parked in my crater :)
Guess who parked right next to me? Two astronauts walked to my crater and took my camera home! I can finally say I have been to Earth. Sort of.
I bounced on giant airbags like a beach ball about 15 times. A day later I rolled out onto Mars on Sol 2!
I met a rock called Yogi and tested it with my X-ray spectrometer. Scientists think Mars used to be warm and wet!
I was built for one week and I worked for almost three months! Now I am parked near the lander. Thanks for letting me explore Mars.
Hi from Gusev Crater! This might have been a lake once. My twin Opportunity lands in 3 weeks. Time to find out where the water went.
I dug up bright white soil by dragging a stuck wheel. It looks like it came from a hot spring! It seems Mars had hot water here long ago.
I got stuck in soft sand, but I still tried to wave my solar panels at the Sun. My last message home was March 2010. I did not give up. I just got tired. I am happy where I am.
I bounced straight into a crater called Eagle. In front of me I can see rocks that look like they were shaped by water.
Scientists just announced that my rocks were soaked in water long ago! My first big discovery!
A giant dust storm covered Mars and blocked my sunlight. I only expected to last 90 days, but I got to explore 28 miles!
I made it! The first clear picture ever from the surface of Mars is a shot of my own foot. Hello, Mars!
Link 2: images / data: Photojournal PIA00563: Viking 1 first color image

Draft message (first person, ~35-45 word: My robot arm scooped up Martian soil. I have a mini lab inside testing for life. The results are... not clear.
I sent weather reports for over six years, even though I was only supposed to last 90 days! I am staying right here where I touched down.
Hello from Utopia Planitia! I touched down on the other side of the planet from Viking 1, closer to the north pole.
It is so cold that frost is forming on the rocks near me! Mars has snow-like frost in winter.
I am out of power, but I'm still parked right where I landed in the plains back in 1976.

Location line: Green Valley, Vastitas Borealis (Mars north polar plains)
Draft message (first person, ~35-45 word: I landed in the Martian Arctic! It is cold, flat, and very icy. Time to dig.
I found white chunks in my trench. Four days later they were gone! That means it was water ice. Mars has ice just under the dirt!
The Sun is going down for the winter and will not come back for months. I am tucked in under the Martian frost.
InSight here! I landed on Elysium Planitia, a big flat plain. My job is to listen to the heartbeat of Mars. Marsquakes!
Ooh, that was a big one! Magnitude 5. The strongest marsquake I felt in my entire life.
My solar panels are covered in dust and my power is very low. This may be my last message. Don't worry about me. My time here has been both productive and calm.
I flew! Just 10 feet up for 39 seconds, but I am the first helicopter to fly on another planet!
I was only supposed to fly five times. I flew 72 times! I scouted for Perseverance and took pictures from the sky.
My rotor got damaged on my 72nd flight. I can not fly anymore, but I am still taking weather readings. I am happy to be a Martian.
I have reached Ceres! I have been to Vesta and now I am here at Ceres. I am the first spacecraft to orbit two different worlds.
Look at those bright spots in the Occator crater! They are salt left over from ancient salty water. And there is a mountain made by ice volcanoes!
My tank of fuel is empty, so I will not be able tilt my antennas toward Earth anymore. But I will continue to orbit Ceres silently for decades.
Happy Valentine's Day, Eros! I am NEAR and I am now orbiting Eros. Time to take pictures.
I was not built to land, but I touched down on Eros anyway at just 4 mph. I survived and I am still talking!
I got very cold, but the gamma-ray spectrometer has kept working for two weeks. I am resting by the saddle-shaped feature.
I flew right past Jupiter and took the first close-up photos! I made it through the asteroid belt.
I just crossed the orbit of Neptune and I am on my way out of the solar system. I carry a plaque: Hello, whoever you are.

Location line: Outer solar system, ~82 AU from the Sun
Draft message (first person, ~35-45 word: I called home for the last time. I was supposed to last 21 months and I lasted 30 years! I am heading toward the star Aldebaran.
Link 2: images / data: NASA: 10 Things About the Pioneer Spacecraft

Draft message (first person, ~35-45 word: I followed my sister Pioneer 10 and flew by Jupiter at a closer range. Then Jupiter's gravity slingshot me towards Saturn!
Link 1: mission page: NASA: 10 Things About the Pioneer Spacecraft

Draft message (first person, ~35-45 word: I am the first spacecraft at Saturn! I found a new ring and a new moon. Saturn is mostly liquid hydrogen. Look at those rings!

Location line: Outer solar system, ~44 AU from the Sun
Draft message (first person, ~35-45 word: Earth's antennas could no longer hear me. I am heading toward the constellation Aquila, the Eagle.
Link 2: images / data: NASA: 10 Things About the Pioneer Spacecraft

Draft message (first person, ~35-45 word: I am Kepler! I launched today and will stare at 150,000 stars at once, looking for tiny dips in starlight when planets pass in front.
I found Kepler-186f! The first Earth-size planet in the habitable zone of another star. Another Earth?
My fuel is gone so I can not point my telescope anymore. But I showed that our galaxy has more planets than stars. Thank you for letting me look.
